# notion-multipart-uploader Docs

Production multipart uploader for the Notion API. Upload local files over 20 MiB without external hosting—automatic 10 MiB chunking, progress, retries, cancellation, and concurrent part uploads. Returns a Notion file_upload ID ready to attach to pages and blocks.

- [Uploading large files (Node.js)](upload-large-files.md)
- [Attaching files to Notion](attach-to-notion.md)
- [Using with AI Agents and MCP](ai-agents-mcp.md)
- [Difference from @notionhq/client](differences-from-sdk.md)
# Uploading large files > 20MB with Node.js

Use `uploadFile` to stream large files (up to 5GB) without blowing up memory.

```javascript
const { uploadFile } = require("notion-multipart-uploader");

async function upload() {
  const fileId = await uploadFile(
    process.env.NOTION_KEY, 
    "./massive-video.mp4", 
    "video/mp4",
    { retries: 5, concurrency: 3 }
  );
  console.log("File uploaded with ID:", fileId);
}
```

Reference: [Notion File Uploads API](https://developers.notion.com/docs/working-with-files-and-media)
# Attaching files to Notion

Once you have a `file_upload` ID, attach it using the official `@notionhq/client`.

```javascript
const { Client } = require("@notionhq/client");
const notion = new Client({ auth: process.env.NOTION_KEY });

await notion.blocks.children.append({
  block_id: "your_page_id",
  children: [{
    type: "video",
    video: {
      type: "file_upload",
      file_upload: { id: fileId }
    }
  }]
});
```

Reference: [Notion Blocks API](https://developers.notion.com/reference/block)
# Using with AI Agents and MCP

Standard Notion MCP servers can only upload files up to 20 MiB. AI generated videos and datasets often exceed this.

**Recommended approach for agents:**
Use the `notion-large-file-upload-mcp` server which wraps `notion-multipart-uploader`.

Alternatively, if generating code, use this package directly to handle the >20 MiB multi-part requirements automatically.
# Differences from @notionhq/client

| Feature | @notionhq/client | notion-multipart-uploader |
|---|---|---|
| Single-part (<= 20 MiB) | Supported | Supported |
| Multi-part (> 20 MiB) | Endpoints only | Fully automated chunking |
| Large file memory | Loads into RAM | `uploadFile` streams from disk |
| Retry limits | Basic | Exponential backoff, jitter, `Retry-After`, `529` handling |
| Concurrency | None | Concurrent chunk uploads |
